title: Mitchell 2024 TTX · HVAA protection
subtitle: Three published lines of effort, Figures 6–8
description: TTX team's three high-value airborne asset protection lines of effort: strike-pulse protection, reactive ambush-alert CCA waves, and decoy/ISR/electronic-attack missions between pulses.
assumptions: LOE names and described roles are sourced to report Figures 6–8 and pp. 19–20, not actual combat operations.
The report names Japan and the Ryukyus as launch/recovery regions, but the site's exact display points and trajectories are illustrative.
The report describes F-22s, E-7A, air-refueling tankers, F-15EX and notional EW, ISR and expendable counterair CCA. Abstract icons must not imply recorded specific sorties.
The planning team proposed using its expendable allocation in the first two days; presentation timestamps are not those days.
No target locations, engagement outcomes, or tactical timings are inferred.

phases.title: LOE 1 · HVAA pulse support
phases.narrative: LOE 1 (Figure 6): CCA screens and F-22s support E-7A and tankers during strike pulses.

phases.title: LOE 2 · Ambush alert
phases.narrative: LOE 2 (Figure 7): reactive expendable counterair CCA supported by recoverable ISR/EW CCA sustain pressure between pulses.

phases.title: LOE 3 · Decoy operations
phases.narrative: LOE 3 (Figure 8): decoy and EW/ISR CCA create uncertainty and help identify targets of opportunity.

phases.title: LOEs recur intermittently
phases.narrative: Editorial presentation reset; the report specifies no such exact reconstitution interval.
